info.description: Read calls, contacts, appointments and messages, book appointments, and subscribe to webhooks. Authenticate with an API key in the Authorization header. A platform key also names the business it acts on in the LobbyStack-Business header. Each key allows 120 requests per minute by default.

post.description: Asks Polar for a page where the customer pays for a plan. Poll GET /billing/checkout/{checkout_id} until status is ready, then send them checkout_url. As in the dashboard, a free business can buy either plan and a Starter business can move to Pro. A Starter business already pays, so its move to Pro needs no page: Polar changes that subscription and charges the difference to the saved payment method, and status becomes changed. Other changes happen in Polar's billing portal and are a 409, as are a managed plan and a plan this deployment doesn't sell. With plan promo and a promo_code, it sells the plan the code unlocks, with that plan's discount, to a free, Starter or Pro business; one that already pays has its subscription moved, as above. A code that doesn't work for the business, for any reason, is a 400 on promo_code. A business can try 10 codes an hour, and a key 20 across the businesses it reaches. With a platform key the checkout is made out to the business's owner, so a business nobody has claimed yet is a 409. Each business has its own Polar customer, made on its first checkout with the payer's email or billing_email. Polar keeps one customer per email, so when the email already belongs to another business's customer the checkout ends in error, and another with a separate billing_email works.
